Amitabh Bachchan received the Lifetime Achievement Award at the 4th Asian Film Awards (Hong Kong, 2010).

Dronavalli Harika is a chess Grandmaster and received the Padma Shri for chess.
Kalli Purie (India Today Group) was honoured with India's Most Powerful Women in Media Award at the Confluence Excellence Award ceremony in the British Parliament in 2019.

Union Civil Aviation Minister K. Rammohan Naidu was named among the World Economic Forum's Young Global Leaders, Class of 2025 (announced April 2025; one of seven Indians among 116 under-40 leaders).

Australian Open 16–29 Jan 2023; Walt Disney Company turned 100 on 16 Oct 2023; Queen Elizabeth II died 8 Sep 2022; FIFA World Cup Qatar ran Nov–18 Dec 2022.

United World Wrestling named Antim Panghal (53 kg) Rising Star of the Year 2023.

Parul Chaudhary ran 8:57.19 at the Sound Running Sunset Tour in Los Angeles on 2 July 2022, becoming the first Indian woman under nine minutes in the 3000m.

'The Scent of God' (2019) is a novel by Saikat Majumdar.
Thomas Kuhn introduced the 'paradigm' idea in The Structure of Scientific Revolutions (1962); Haggett, Wright and Von Thunen are geographers.

'Cry, the Peacock' is the 1963 novel by Anita Desai.
Rishikesh in Uttarakhand is known as the 'Yoga Capital of the World'.

'Nineteen Eighty-Four' is the dystopian novel by George Orwell.
'Born Again on the Mountain' is by Arunima Sinha, the amputee mountaineer who climbed Everest.
'Citizen and Society' is a book by former Vice-President Hamid Ansari.
Army Day is 15 January (Gen. K.M. Cariappa took over as first Indian C-in-C in 1949); 4 December is Navy Day and 7 December Armed Forces Flag Day.
'Revolution 2020' is a novel by Chetan Bhagat.
'A Passage to India' (1924) was written by E.M. Forster.
Earth Day is observed on 22 April every year (since 1970). 22 March is World Water Day and 22 May the Biodiversity Day.
"The Coming China Wars" (2006) is by Peter Navarro, the US economist and later trade adviser.
World Braille Day is observed on 4 January, the birthday of Louis Braille.
'India Shastra: Reflections on the Nation in Our Time' is by Shashi Tharoor.
'A Brief History of Time' (1988) was written by the physicist Stephen Hawking.
'Adhe-Adhure' is a Hindi play by Mohan Rakesh.
'By the skin of your teeth' means just barely (narrowly escaping).
Angola became independent from Portugal on 11 November 1975, commemorated as its Independence Day every year.
'The Audacity of Hope' (2006) is by Barack Obama, later US President.
The Satanic Verses (1988) is Salman Rushdie's novel; his other major works include Midnight's Children and Victory City.
'A Bend in the River' (1979) is a novel by V.S. Naipaul.
International Volunteer Day is observed on 5 December (UN, since 1985).
'An Area of Darkness' (1964) is by V.S. Naipaul; the other three are Rushdie's works.
'The Hungry Tide' is a novel by Amitav Ghosh set in the Sundarbans.
The 'A Song of Ice and Fire' series, adapted as 'Game of Thrones', is by George R.R. Martin.
National Postal Day is 10 October (part of National Postal Week); World Post Day is 9 October.
'The Kashmir Dispute 1947-2012' (2 vols, Tulika, 2013) is by A.G. Noorani, constitutional expert and commentator.
'The Unseen Indira Gandhi' was written by Dr K.P. Mathur, her personal physician.
'Turning Points: A Journey Through Challenges' was written by APJ Abdul Kalam as a sequel to 'Wings of Fire'.
'And Then One Day: A Memoir' is the autobiography of actor Naseeruddin Shah.
The International Diabetes Federation's World Diabetes Day theme for 2018-2019 was 'The Family and Diabetes'.
